gallery.title: File:Solomon Juneau.jpg
gallery.credit: Created and originally uploaded to the English Wikipedia by Sulfur.
gallery.description:
Memorial statue of city founder Solomon Juneau, located on the grounds of Juneau Park in Milwaukee, Wisconsin.


This statue, located in Juneau Park, was the gift of shoe manufacturers Charles T. Bradley and William H. Metcalf. Juneau's granddaughter Hattie White unveiled the statue on July 6, 1887. Artist Richard Henry Park created the sculpture.

gallery.filename: Milwaukee (WIS) Downtown Riverwalk 100 East Building & First National Bank Building (4743909231).jpg
gallery.title: File:Milwaukee (WIS) Downtown Riverwalk 100 East Building & First National Bank Building (4743909231).jpg
gallery.credit: Milwaukee (WIS) Downtown Riverwalk 100 East Building & First National Bank Building
gallery.source: Milwaukee (WIS) Downtown Riverwalk 100 East Building & First National Bank Building (4743909231)
gallery.description:
100 East Building
1989

An example of postmodern architecture with consideration for the neighborhood in which it resides. The 37 stories are built of cream colored Cordoba (Texas) limestone with deep brown metal spandrels and tinted glass. It is on the site of the former Pabst Building.

First National Bank Building
735 N. Water St.
Built: 1914
This served as the headquarters of the First Wisconsin National Bank until the completion of the Firstar Center in 1973. The lower floors are granite, with the upper floors pressed buff brick.

gallery.title: File:1950 Flag DesignWinner.jpg
gallery.description: A black-and-white rendition of the winning design in Milwaukee's 1950 flag design contest. It features a ribbon with the name "Milwaukee" over three gears labeled "HOMES", "INDUSTRY", and "SHIPPING".  This design was never officially adopted by the city, though some elements were later re-purposed for Milwaukee's first official flag in 1954.
